verses.1:1: James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes that are in the Dispersion: Greetings.
verses.1:2: Regard it as complete joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials,
verses.1:3: knowing that the testing of your faith brings about endurance.
verses.1:4: And let endurance have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and whole, lacking nothing.
verses.1:5: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from God, who gives to everyone generously and without rebuking, and it will be given to him.
verses.1:6: Yet let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a surge of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed about.
verses.1:7: For that person must not expect that he will receive anything from the Lord,
verses.1:8: a double-minded man, unstable in all of his ways.
verses.1:9: Now let the humble brother boast in his high position,
verses.1:10: and the rich one in his humbling, because like a blossom of the grass he will pass away.
verses.1:11: For the sun rises with its scorching heat and dries up the grass, and its blossom falls off, and the beauty of its appearance perishes; in the same way the rich man also will fade away in his pursuits.
verses.1:12: Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because having been approved, he will receive the crown of life, which He promised to those who love Him.
verses.1:13: When anyone is tempted, let him not say, "I am tempted by God," for God cannot be tempted by evil, and He Himself does not tempt anyone.
verses.1:14: Rather, each one is tempted as he is drawn away and lured by his own desire.
verses.1:15: Then, once desire has conceived, it bears sin; and when sin is fully formed, it brings forth death.
verses.1:16: Do not be misled, my beloved brothers.
verses.1:17: Every good giving and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of the lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
verses.1:18: By His own choice He brought us forth by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
verses.1:19: Know this, my beloved brothers. And every person must be quick to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
verses.1:20: for a man's anger does not accomplish God's righteousness.
verses.1:21: Therefore, laying aside all filthiness and abundance of malice, welcome with gentleness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
verses.1:22: And become doers of the word, and not hearers only, deluding yourselves.
verses.1:23: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, this person resembles a man observing his natural face in a mirror;
verses.1:24: for he observes himself and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of person he was.
verses.1:25: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and continues in it, becoming not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this one will be blessed in his doing.
verses.1:26: If anyone thinks he is religious while not bridling his tongue, but deceiving his own heart, this person's religion is worthless.
verses.1:27: Pure and undefiled religion in the sight of God the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.
verses.2:1: My brothers, surely you do not hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with acts of partiality?
verses.2:2: For if a man wearing a gold ring comes into your assembly in fine clothing, and a poor man in dirty clothing also comes in,
verses.2:3: and you pay special attention to the one wearing the fine clothing and say, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You stand over there, or sit below my footstool,"
verses.2:4: have you not drawn distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil reasoning?
verses.2:5: Listen, my beloved brothers. Did God not choose those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom He promised to those who love Him?
verses.2:6: Yet you have dishonored the poor man. Do the rich not oppress you, and are they not the ones dragging you into the courts?
verses.2:7: Do they not blaspheme the noble name that was invoked over you?
verses.2:8: If, however, you are fulfilling the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
verses.2:9: Yet if you show partiality, you commit sin, convicted by the law as transgressors.
verses.2:10: For anyone who keeps the entire law, yet stumbles in a single point, has become guilty of all.
verses.2:11: For He who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." Now if you do not commit adultery, yet you do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
verses.2:12: Speak in this way and act in this way, as those who are about to be judged through the law of freedom.
verses.2:13: For judgment is merciless to the one who did not show mercy; mercy triumphs over judgment.
verses.2:14: What is the benefit, my brothers, if someone says he has faith, yet has no works? Can that faith save him?
verses.2:15: If a brother or a sister is without clothing and lacking daily food,
verses.2:16: and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, keep warm and be well fed," yet you do not give them what is needed for the body, what is the benefit?
verses.2:17: In the same way, faith also, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.
verses.2:18: Yet someone will say, "You have faith, and I have works." Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you faith by my works.
verses.2:19: Do you believe that God is one? You are doing well; the demons also believe, and they shudder.
verses.2:20: But do you want to know, you empty person, that faith apart from works is useless?
verses.2:21: Was Abraham our father not justified by works when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
verses.2:22: You see that faith was working together with his works, and by works faith was perfected,
verses.2:23: and the Scripture was fulfilled that says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and he was called a friend of God.
verses.2:24: You see that a person is justified by works, and not by faith only.
verses.2:25: And in the same way, was Rahab the prostitute not also justified by works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them out by another road?
verses.2:26: For just as the body apart from spirit is dead, so too faith apart from works is dead.
verses.3:1: Do not let many of you become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
verses.3:2: For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in word, this person is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body as well.
verses.3:3: Now if we put bits into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, we guide their entire body as well.
verses.3:4: Look at ships also: though they are so great and are driven by fierce winds, they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the pilot wills.
verses.3:5: In the same way, the tongue also is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. See how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest!
verses.3:6: And the tongue is a fire; as the world of unrighteousness, the tongue is placed among our members, staining the entire body and setting ablaze the wheel of existence, while itself being set ablaze by Gehenna.
verses.3:7: For every kind of wild beast and bird, of reptile and sea creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind,
verses.3:8: but no human being is able to tame the tongue; it is an unstable evil, full of deadly poison.
verses.3:9: With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made according to the likeness of God.
verses.3:10: From the same mouth come forth blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
verses.3:11: Does a spring gush both fresh water and bitter from the same opening?
verses.3:12: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine yield figs? Neither can salt water yield fresh water.
verses.3:13: Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him demonstrate his works from a good way of life in the gentleness of wisdom.
verses.3:14: Yet if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast arrogantly and lie against the truth.
verses.3:15: This is not wisdom coming down from above; rather, it is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
verses.3:16: For wherever jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is disorder and every base deed.
verses.3:17: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, considerate, open to persuasion, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, and without hypocrisy.
verses.3:18: And fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.
verses.4:1: Where do wars come from, and where do fights among you come from? Is it not from this, from your pleasures that wage war in your members?
verses.4:2: You desire and do not have; you murder and are envious, and you are not able to obtain; you fight and wage war. You do not have because you do not ask.
verses.4:3: You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, in order to spend it on your pleasures.
verses.4:4: Adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore, whoever intends to be a friend of the world is made an enemy of God.
verses.4:5: Or do you suppose that the Scripture speaks in vain, "He jealously longs for the spirit that He caused to dwell in us"?
verses.4:6: But He gives greater grace; therefore it says, "God opposes the proud, yet to the humble He gives grace."
verses.4:7: Be subject therefore to God, but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
verses.4:8: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, double-minded ones.
verses.4:9: Be distressed, and mourn, and weep; let your laughter be changed into mourning, and your joy into dejection.
verses.4:10: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and He will exalt you.
verses.4:11: Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one speaking against a brother or judging his brother speaks against the law and judges the law; and if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
verses.4:12: There is one Lawgiver and Judge, the One able to save and to destroy; but who are you, the one judging your neighbor?
verses.4:13: Come now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, and spend a year there, and carry on trade, and make a profit,"
verses.4:14: you who do not know what belongs to tomorrow, what your life is like—for you are a mist that appears for a short time and then disappears—
verses.4:15: instead of your saying, "If the Lord wills, we will both live and do this or that."
verses.4:16: But as it is, you boast in your arrogant pretensions; all boasting of this kind is evil.
verses.4:17: Therefore, for the one who knows to do what is good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
verses.5:1: Come now, you rich, weep, wailing over your miseries that are coming.
verses.5:2: Your wealth has rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten,
verses.5:3: your gold and your silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh; like fire you have stored up treasure in the last days.
verses.5:4: Look, the pay of the laborers who mowed your fields, which was kept back by you, cries out, and the outcries of those who harvested have entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
verses.5:5: You lived in luxury on the earth and gave yourselves to pleasure; you fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.
verses.5:6: You condemned, you murdered the righteous one. Does he not oppose you?
verses.5:7: Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until it receives the early and late rain.
verses.5:8: Be patient, you also; strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
verses.5:9: Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged; look, the Judge is standing before the doors.
verses.5:10: Take as an example, brothers, of suffering hardship and of patience, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
verses.5:11: Look, we consider blessed those who endured. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the outcome from the Lord, that the Lord is very compassionate and merciful.
verses.5:12: Now above all, my brothers, do not swear—neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath; instead, let your "Yes" be yes and your "No" be no, so that you may not fall under judgment.
verses.5:13: Is anyone among you suffering hardship? Let him pray. Is anyone in good spirits? Let him sing praises.
verses.5:14: Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;
verses.5:15: and the prayer of faith will save the ailing person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
verses.5:16: Therefore confess your sins to one another, and pray on behalf of one another, so that you may be healed. The petition of a righteous person has great power in its working.
verses.5:17: Elijah was a man of like nature with us, and he prayed earnestly for it not to rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months;
verses.5:18: and he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
verses.5:19: My brothers, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
verses.5:20: let him know that the one who turns back a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

notes.1:13: The Greek verb peirazo (and noun peirasmos in 1:2, 1:12) can mean either "test/trial" or "tempt/temptation" depending on context; here James shifts from outward trials to inward solicitation to evil.
notes.1:17: "Variation" (parallage) and "shadow of turning" (tropes aposkiasma) draw on ancient astronomical terms describing the shifting movements and shadows of heavenly bodies.
notes.1:23: Literally "the face of his birth," a Greek idiom for one's natural face.
notes.2:1: The verb echete can be read as a question ("surely you do not hold...?") matching the Greek punctuation here, or as an imperative ("do not hold..."); "our glorious Lord Jesus Christ" is literally "our Lord Jesus Christ of glory." The Greek genitive phrase τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ("the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ") can be understood either objectively as "faith in our Lord Jesus Christ" or subjectively as "the faithfulness of our Lord Jesus Christ."
notes.2:14: The Greek definite article before "faith" (he pistis) points back to the claimed, workless faith just mentioned, hence "that faith."
notes.2:18: Commentators debate whether the hypothetical speaker's quotation ends after "I have works" (as punctuated here) or continues through the end of the verse.
notes.2:20: The Greek creates a wordplay between ergon ("works") and arge ("useless" or "barren," literally "workless").
notes.2:26: The Greek noun pneuma can be rendered either "spirit" or "breath."
notes.3:6: "The wheel of existence" (ton trochon tes geneseos) is literally "the wheel of origin (or birth)," a metaphor for the whole course of human life.
notes.3:18: The Greek dative tois poiousin eirenen can be understood either as "for those who make peace" (dative of advantage) or "by those who make peace" (dative of agency).
notes.4:4: "Adulteresses" is feminine plural in Greek, echoing Old Testament prophetic imagery of spiritual unfaithfulness to God.
notes.4:5: Both the Greek syntax and the exact scriptural source are debated; the quotation can also be rendered "The spirit that He caused to dwell in us longs toward envy," and "spirit" may alternatively refer to the Holy Spirit.
notes.4:14: The Greek phrasing is notably abrupt ("what belongs to tomorrow, what your life is like"), and "you are a mist" follows the critical text's second-person plural verb rather than a variant reading "it is."
notes.5:3: Following the critical text's punctuation, "like fire" modifies "you have stored up treasure," though it is also commonly attached to the preceding clause ("will eat your flesh like fire").
notes.5:4: "Sabaoth" is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning "hosts" or "armies."
notes.5:6: The final clause is punctuated as a question in the critical text ("Does he not oppose you?"), though many interpreters read it as a statement ("He does not oppose you").
notes.5:11: "The outcome from the Lord" translates literally "the end of the Lord," referring to the final result the Lord brought about for Job.
notes.5:16: The Greek participle rendered "in its working" is grammatically ambiguous between a middle sense ("as it operates") and a passive sense ("as it is made effective" by God).
